prompt:
You run weekly onboarding A/B tests. Here is every finished test so far: what you predicted
and what was measured.

- round 1: Interactive Pet Creator Grid [adoption, redesign]: predicted +10.0%, measured +0.6% ± 3.7%, after noise correction +0.2%, lost: no clear effect
- round 2: Postpone Account Sign In [sign_in, reorder]: predicted +8.0%, measured +6.6% ± 2.6%, after noise correction +3.7%, won

By kind of change, after noise correction:
- adoption, redesign: +0.2% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)
- sign_in, reorder: +3.7% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)

One test is weak evidence. State a rule only when at least 2 tests of that kind agree after noise correction; otherwise say the evidence is still thin.

Previous lessons:
Evidence is still thin across all change types with only one test completed so far.

Rewrite the lessons: at most 6 short rules about which kinds of change worked, which did not, and
where your predictions were too high or too low. Call a kind of change helpful only if a test of that
kind won (was significant); for tests with no clear effect, say no effect was seen, even if the numbers
lean one way. Keep rules that still hold, drop ones the data contradicts. Return JSON {"lessons": ["..."]}

lessons: Evidence is still thin for both adoption redesigns and sign-in reordering, as only one test has been completed for each kind of change.
